issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Ride.abbreviation as type 'char', but the solution declares the attribute and getter as String (private String abbreviation; constructor Ride(String, String)). This is an attribute type mismatch that affects the constructor and getter signatures and will confuse students about the expected type for the abbreviation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Ride.abbreviation attribute type consistent with the UML: change the attribute and its getter/constructor parameter to char (private char abbreviation; public Ride(String name, char abbreviation); public char getAbbreviation()). Update all subclasses and usages to accept and pass a char for abbreviation.

issues.description: The problem requires Ride's constructor to accept (name, char abbreviation) (superclass attributes first). The solution's Ride constructor uses (String name, String abbreviation), so the constructor parameter types do not match the specification in the UML. This mismatch will prevent students from implementing subclasses and from matching the expected signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Ride constructor signature to use a char for abbreviation (public Ride(String name, char abbreviation)) to match the UML. Ensure subclasses' constructors take the superclass parameters first and pass them to super(...) with the correct types.

issues.description: RollerCoaster and the launched subclasses in the solution use constructor parameter lists that mix char and String for the abbreviation: RollerCoaster declares (String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) but calls super(name, abbreviation) where the superclass Ride in the solution currently expects a String. This inconsistency between superclass and subclass constructor parameter types will cause compilation errors and confuses the required parameter ordering and types described in the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure a consistent abbreviation type across the hierarchy: make Ride accept a char abbreviation, and update RollerCoaster and all subclasses to use (String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) and to call super(name, abbreviation) where the types match. Alternatively, if the design intentionally requires String, update the UML/problem statement to reflect String consistently.

issues.description: The UML/problem specification defines Ride.abbreviation as type 'char' (abbreviation: char), but the solution implementation declares Ride.abbreviation as a String and the Ride constructor/ getter use String. This mismatch between the specified type and the implemented type for the same conceptual attribute can confuse students about the expected data type and constructor signatures across the artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of 'abbreviation' consistent across problem, template, and solution. Either change the UML/spec to use String for abbreviation, or update the solution (and template) to declare 'private char abbreviation', adjust the Ride constructor parameter to 'char abbreviation', and change the getter to return char. Ensure all subclasses and constructors use the same abbreviation type.
